Baltic Seal.png.taxonomy_note: Asset is named Baltic Seal, but scientific_name is species-level Pusa hispida; Nearctic mapping follows the full species (Ringed Seal), not only Baltic subspecies P. h. botnica.

Western Barn Owl.png.taxonomy_geography_note: Scientific name Tyto alba is Western Barn Owl under the modern split; New World barn owls are American Barn Owl Tyto furcata.

Eurasian Goshawk.png.taxonomy_geography_note: Scientific name Accipiter gentilis is Eurasian Goshawk under the modern split; North American populations are American Goshawk Accipiter atricapillus, a separate species.

Peregrine Falcon.png.bioregion_safetynet_note: Southern Patagonia/Tierra del Fuego use is not strong enough here to assign the broad NT2 polygon under the conservative seasonal-living rule.

Steller's Sea Eagle.png.taxonomy_geography_note: Native breeding/resident range is northeastern Asia; Alaska/North American records are vagrancy/exceptional occurrence and do not meet the project's true-living-range rule.

Striated Caracara.png.bioregion_safetynet_note: Retained: far-southern Patagonia/Tierra del Fuego/Falklands are the species core.

Turkey Vulture.png.bioregion_safetynet_note: Regular South American range reaches Patagonia, but the far-southern NT2 polygon was too broad under the conservative bioregion rule.

Andean Condor.png.bioregion_safetynet_note: Retained: core resident range genuinely extends through Patagonian Andes to Tierra del Fuego.

Ferruginous Pygmy Owl.png.geography_note: Resident widespread Neotropical owl; mapping includes Sonoran/Texan drylands, Central America, seasonally flooded western Amazon, Chaco/Cerrado and Atlantic Forest habitats; dense unflooded Amazon forest is not treated as universal habitat.

Short-Eared Owl.png.bioregion_safetynet_note: Retained: Short-eared Owl has genuine open-country populations in Patagonia/Tierra del Fuego and island populations, so southern IDs remain defensible.

American Barn Owl.png.bioregion_safetynet_note: American Barn Owl reaches far southern South America, but NT2 as a whole overstates established habitat; retain more defensible adjacent/open-country regions.

notes.geography: Animal geography is stored in wild_regions (One Earth), marine_regions (MEOW), and pelagic_regions (PPOW), not duplicated as continent/subregion tags.
notes.composition: Habitat tags are compositional: for example, swamp forest is represented by a forest tag plus wetland rather than a separate swamp tag.
notes.categoryAndLevel: Category and rarity level remain encoded by the Category -> Level hierarchy.

zooTypeWeights.typeSelectionRule: Zoo type comes from the grouped zoo-name prefix database; unrecognized/custom names default to general unless the player explicitly selects a type.

general.description: No collection bias; baseline weighting for a general zoological collection.

aquarium.description: Aquatic specialist. Strongly favours aquatic animals; also mildly favours wetland, semi-aquatic and tropical species, with a small reptile overlap from aquatic/terrarium husbandry.

tropical.description: Climate-controlled tropical collection. Favours rainforest species, with natural secondary overlap into reptiles, small mammals and tropical aquatic/semi-aquatic exhibits.

safari.description: Large open-range collection. Favours African savanna ungulates most strongly, with weaker preferences for associated carnivores, large birds and dry-country species.

forest.description: Woodland collection. Favours temperate/boreal forest fauna, with smaller biases toward woodland carnivores, ungulates and forest-wetland species.

farm.description: Domestic and contact-animal collection. Domestic status dominates; ungulates and familiar temperate mammals receive only small secondary preferences.

bird.description: Bird specialist with aviaries and climate-controlled houses. Strongly favours all bird categories, with modest wetland/tropical overlap and only a very small reptile-house crossover.

reptile.description: Mostly indoor terrarium specialist. Strongly favours reptiles, but its heated indoor exhibits and aquarium/terrarium expertise also make tropical, aquatic, semi-aquatic, desert and nocturnal species more likely.

alpine.description: Mountain collection. Strongly favours mountain fauna, with smaller cold-climate and mountain-associated ungulate, carnivore and raptor preferences.

raptor.description: Raptor and falconry specialist. Very strongly favours Birds of Prey while retaining a small chance of other bird groups and habitat-associated species.

incomingTradeOffers.rule: For each category/tag multiplier M above, use 1 + ((M - 1) * tradePreferenceStrength). This preserves the same preference direction but makes incoming offers less type-dominated than starting generation.

notes: Category and tag bonuses stack multiplicatively, then are capped.
No type excludes animals: a non-matching animal retains baseline weight 1.0.
Level/rarity is deliberately not part of zoo-type weighting; existing game progression rules continue to control levels.
Continent tags are currently used directly only by safari (Africa). They remain available for later regional/specialist zoo types.
Nocturnal is retained as animal metadata for a future nocturnal-house or nocturnal-zoo preference; it is not forced into an unrelated current type.

Logic pass v2 adds restrained secondary preferences based on likely facilities and husbandry expertise (e.g. reptile zoos also favour tropical and aquatic animals). Primary identity bonuses remain substantially stronger than crossover bonuses.
